items.title: MacKinnon has four points as Avalanche beat Lightning
items.summary: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Nazem Kadri scored his first goal of the season and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 on Friday night.
items.body: DENVER — Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Nazem Kadri scored his first goal of the season and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 on Friday night. Devon Toews, Fedor Svechkov, Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas also scored as Colorado rebounded from back-to-back road losses. Mackenzie Blackwood made 31 saves. Jake Guentzel scored twice and Charle-Edouard D’Astous added another for the Lightning, who saw their three-game winning streak halted. Nikita Kucherov was held in check and remains a goal or assist away from becoming the franchise's career points leader. He has 1,137 points and is tied with Steven Stamkos. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 18 of 23 shots, including one off the mask on MacKinnon's liner. Guentzel's goal with 42.7 seconds left in the second period made it 4-2. The Avalanche unsuccessfully challenged the play for a missed stoppage. The Lightning went on the power play but couldn't score. They struggled on the power play all evening. MacKinnon’s goal with 15:42 remaining gave Colorado a 5-2 cushion. Necas sealed it with a late empty-net tally. Logan O’Connor returned to the lineup after missing the start of the season with a lower-body injury. He recently lost his father, Myles, a former NHL defenseman, at age 59. The game featured the league's currently longest-tenured coaches in Jon Cooper and Jared Bednar. Cooper took over the Lightning in March 2013 and has won two Stanley Cups. Bednar was hired by Colorado in August 2016 and captured one Cup — in 2022 over the Lightning. Wyndham Clark, the 2026 U.S. Open champion, was in attendance and brought his trophy. Clark drank from the cup while receiving an ovation from the crowd.

items.title: Evans scores twice to lead Canadiens over Blackhawks
items.body: CHICAGO — Jake Evans scored twice and assisted on Kaiden Guhle’s goal and the Montreal Canadiens beat the Chicago Blackhawks 4-1 on Friday night. Evans’ third point, a feed to Guhle with 1:34 left in the second period, matched his career high. Montreal is 4-1-1 in its last six games, while Chicago has dropped two straight and four of its last six. A wide-open game tightened up late in the first period, which worked to Montreal’s advantage. Chicago opened the scoring on Connor Bedard ’s second goal of the season 4:23 in, but the Canadiens began to control the play, and by mid-period were limiting Chicago’s chances. Jacob Fowler, who made 20 saves, was lightly tested the rest of the game despite five Chicago power plays, and needed to make only three saves in the final period. Evans’ first goal of the game and season tied it with 2:31 left in the first. His second, a wrist shot over goalie Spencer Knight’s stick side with the Canadiens skating short-handed, gave Montreal a 2-1 lead 7:51 into the second period. Guhle also beat Knight on the stick side, his shot from the left point screened by Josh Anderson. Canadiens: At Winnipeg on Sunday for the outdoor Heritage Classic.

Still, Larkin hasn’t budged so far, at least in the Canadian market. Originally listing the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, and Vegas Golden Knights, Larkin has since expanded his list to include the Carolina Hurricanes, Colorado Avalanche, Dallas Stars, New Jersey Devils, Tampa Bay Lightning, Utah Mammoth, and Washington Capitals. The complicating factor is that every team on Larkin’s list has limited cap space and would essentially need to execute a money-in, money-out deal. However, he received a warm reception in Detroit’s first matchup in Montreal this year. On the off-chance he expands his list to include the Canadiens, a deal should come together relatively quickly. In a corresponding roster move, the Ducks placed defenseman Pavel Mintyukov on the injured reserve with a lower-body ailment. Mitchell’s demotion didn’t last long. The 26-year-old blueliner began the year on Anaheim’s blue line but was reassigned on October 11th. In his five games with the Ducks, Mitchell went scoreless, earning a -3 rating and averaging 16:36 of ice time per game. It’s been a similar story with AHL San Diego. Since Mitchell was demoted a week and a half ago, he has gone scoreless in four contests with an identical -3 rating. Anaheim signed Mitchell to a one-year, $850K contract this past offseason after he became a Group VI unrestricted free agent. Meanwhile, the Ducks have lost one of their better-skilled defenseman for at least another week. Mintyukov, 23, signed a five-year, $36MM ($7.2MM AAV) contract on July 5th, making him Anaheim’s second-highest-paid defenseman. He has registered two assists in nine games for the Ducks this season. Unfortunately, Anaheim doesn’t have room for error with their defensive corps. The Ducks lost John Carlson , Jacob Trouba , and Radko Gudas to unrestricted free agency this past summer, and replaced most of them internally. Now, without Mintyukov and Ian Moore , Anaheim will have to make do with their other options.

items.summary: Edmonton recalled goaltender Matt Tomkins from the AHL on an emergency basis.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Edmonton Oilers announced Friday that goaltender Devon Levi has been placed on injured reserve. The team also announced they have recalled goaltender Matt Tomkins from their AHL affiliate, the Bakersfield Condors, under emergency conditions. Levi missed practice with the team on Friday, and according to Oilers Now reporter Bob Stauffer, Tristan Jarry will get the start Saturday against the Toronto Maple Leafs . Through seven games, Levi posted a 6-1-0 record with an .887 save percentage (SV%) and 3.11 goals against average (GAA). In 46 career NHL games, the native of Dollard-des-Ormeaux, Que., is 23-18-2 with an .893 SV% and 3.26 GAA with the Oilers and Buffalo Sabres . Levi, a seventh-round pick for the Florida Panthers in 2020, has appeared in 120 regular-season AHL games with the Rochester Americans across three seasons. He’s posted a 64-39-22 record with a .914 SV% and 2.52 GAA. He also played three seasons of college hockey with Northeastern University. In 66 career NCAA games, he went 38-22-6 with a .942 SV% and 1.90 GAA. As for Tomkins, the 32-year-old netminder has appeared in eight AHL seasons, where he’s posted a 59-57-19 record with a .903 SV% and 2.89 GAA. He’s also appeared in six career NHL games. The Oilers are 8-1-1 through their first 10 games of the 2026-27 regular season. They defeated the Carolina Hurricanes 6-5 in a shootout Thursday, thanks to a pair of five-point performances from captain Connor McDavid and forward Leon Draisaitl. They will host the Leafs Saturday. Puck drop is at 7 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. MT.

items.body: WINNIPEG — From an unheralded teenager playing in Odessa, Texas, plucked out of the fifth round, to becoming one of the premier goaltenders in the world. And what a circus it became over the last few months, as the Winnipeg Jets navigated the delicate nuances of trying to move a franchise cornerstone in a market plagued with contractual roadblocks, all while operating inside a goaltending market that almost always favours buyers. All of that finally came to a head on Friday, when the Jets traded Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils for a package that included immediate forward help, a couple of high-end prospects and some draft picks. "We drafted Connor Hellebuyck," Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said Friday during a nearly 30-minute press conference at the Canada Life Centre. "We took a chance on some gangly guy out of Odessa. But he's earned his way along the way. As an organization, we're proud of what we had accomplished; we wished we could have pushed it over the top." items.title: Mammoth sign Artem Duda to two-year contract extension
items.summary: The Utah Mammoth keep faith in Artem Duda’s rise with a new deal through the 2028-29 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Utah Mammoth has signed defenseman Artem Duda to a two-year contract extension, the hockey club announced Friday afternoon. The new deal will begin in the 2027-28 season and run through the end of 2028-29, with the first year as a two-way deal that will see him earn $900,000 in the NHL and $175,000 in the minors, with at least $220,000 guaranteed. In the second year of the contract, the deal becomes a one-way agreement, and he will be paid $950,000. Now 22 years old, Duda has played in parts of three American Hockey League seasons with the Tucson Roadrunners, scoring nine goals and 36 assists for 45 points over 103 regular-season games since entering the professional ranks. Initially selected in the second round of the 2022 NHL Draft by the Arizona Coyotes, Duda began his career in the CSKA Moskva development system and rose to play 14 KHL games in 2022-23, scoring three assists. After his brief KHL stint, the Coyotes looked to bring Duda to North America, but they couldn’t bring a Russian player into the CHL and couldn’t bring a teenager into the AHL. With limited options, the Coyotes worked out a deal with U Sports’ Toronto Metropolitan University, making Duda a rare NHL-drafted prospect to play in Canadian university hockey competitions. With the TMU Bold, he scored two goals and five assists in 12 games, helping the team advance to the national semifinal on home ice, before moving on to the AHL. Currently playing with Tucson, Duda has three points in six AHL games this season, with the Roadrunners sitting at 3-2-1, good for fifth in the AHL’s Pacific Division. He will look to make his NHL debut at some point in 2026-27, or in the next two years, as part of his newly signed deal.

items.body: Mercer, Daws among those going to Winnipeg for three-time Vezina winner, who asked to be dealt in offseason WINNIPEG -- Kevin Cheveldayoff said he can get some sleep again after the Winnipeg Jets general manager completed a trade that sent star goalie Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils on Friday. “I’m very comfortable (with) what we accomplished here over the period of time,” Cheveldayoff said. “I certainly wish we could have done it four months ago, or whatever, when the opportunity started and we were looking (for a trade), but here we are here today.” Winnipeg acquired forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to forward Alexander Command , a second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft. The trade ended the saga that started with Hellebuyck requesting a trade out of Winnipeg during the offseason. He was going into the third season of a seven-year, $59.5 million contract ($8.5 million average annual value) he signed on Oct. 9, 2023. “We want to thank Connor Hellebuyck on behalf of the fans of Winnipeg and the Winnipeg Jets,” Cheveldayoff said. “We had lots of good memories, and I choose to remember those as we continue to move forward. That’s what I talked to Connor about today when I called him and wished him all the best. So, thank you very much to him and all his family.” The Jets suspended Hellebuyck on Sept. 16 for not reporting to training camp. The suspension was scheduled to end Friday. The trade came with the Jets getting ready to play the Montreal Canadiens outdoors in the 2026 Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium here on Sunday (7 p.m. ET; TVAS, SN, TNT, truTV, HBO MAX). Hellebuyck was selected by Winnipeg in the fifth round (No. 130) of the 2012 NHL Draft

items.body: Register Login Blackhawks Activate Andrew Mangiapane By Brennan McClain | at October 23, 2026 5:33 pm The Chicago Blackhawks will have a healthy forward corps against the Montreal Canadiens tonight. The Blackhawks announced they have activated veteran winger Andrew Mangiapane from the injured reserve. Mangiapane, 30, has been on the injured reserve since Chicago’s opening-night contest of the 2026-27 campaign. The middle-six winger has been recovering from a lower-body injury since then. In his one appearance this season, Mangiapane went scoreless before leaving early due to the injury. Unfortunately, just because he is healthy doesn’t necessarily mean Mangiapane will play tonight. The Blackhawks had an opening on their 23-man roster, so no corresponding roster move was needed. Chicago will likely look to see how he feels during warm-ups. As Mario Tirabassi of CHGO Blackhawks correctly points out, activating a player this close to game time makes it more than likely he will play. Mangiapane is in his first full season with the Blackhawks. Beginning last season with the Edmonton Oilers, Mangiapane struggled to find consistent ice time. He ended his tenure with the Oilers having scored seven goals and 14 points in 52 games. A year earlier, with the Washington Capitals, Mangiapane tallied 14 goals and 28 points in 81 contests. He was sent to the Blackhawks at the trade deadline along with a 2027 first-round pick for Colton Dach and Jason Dickinson . He finished the year scoring a goal and an assist in 10 games with his new club.

items.title: Official Opposition Leader Pierre Poilievre Latest To Tour Roustan Sports
items.summary: Today’s tour by the conservative leader followed visits from federal ministers Evan Solomon and Adam van Koeverden, making it three high-profile Canadian politicians on site at the Brantford, Ont., stick factory in less than two months.
items.body: Stephanie Bevan Stephanie Bevan Official Opposition Leader Pierre Poilievre Latest To Tour Roustan Sports Michael Traikos Partner Oct 23, 2026 9:39 PM Published Oct 23, 2026 9:39 PM Today’s tour by the conservative leader followed visits from federal ministers Evan Solomon and Adam van Koeverden, making it three high-profile Canadian politicians on site at the Brantford, Ont., stick factory in less than two months. Pierre Poilievre, the leader of the conservative party of Canada, visited Roustan Sports' stick factory on Friday, where he praised the Brantford, Ont., employees for carrying on a Canadian tradition in the midst of the U.S. trade war. Poilievre is the latest politician to visit the manufacturing facility, which is the sole wooden hockey stick manufacturing facility in Canada — and where 400,000 traditional wood sticks are manufactured yearly. Earlier this month, Adam van Koeverden , Canada’s Secretary of State (Sport), toured the Roustan Sports headquarters. Federal minister Evan Solomon visited in August. Poilievre was accompanied by Brantford mayor Kevin Davis, who will be running for the local Conservative Party of Canada seat in a yet-to-be-announced by-election. As Roustan Sports owner and CEO W. Graeme Roustan explained to media, Davis has been a supporter of the business since Roustan moved the factory from Hespeler, Ont. to Brantford in 2021. “All politicians in Canada recognize that hockey is not only our sport but the culture of our country," Roustan told the Brantford Expositor. “Having the only hockey stick factory in Canada creates a bit of a buzz. "They want to see this place, and walk the factory to see where hockey sticks are made. It’s really an experience.”

items.title: ‘Win today’: How Babcock’s honest, day-by-day approach has worked for Oilers
items.summary: Blunt. To the point. And when it comes to things hockey related, usually right. That’s what they told us we’d be getting when the Oilers brought in Mike Babcock, and so far, the advanced billing has been spot on.
items.body: EDMONTON — A month into the Mike Babcock era, we’re still waiting for a more telling exchange than the one our Elliotte Friedman had with Leon Draisaitl the day before training camp opened. Friedman: “What’s the most honest thing Mike Babcock has said to you so far?” We’ve all hated Draisaitl’s line changes here in Edmonton — but only for about 12 seasons and 856 career NHL games. Yet, it’s Babcock who watched some summer video and brought that back as his first take as Draisaitl’s new coach. Blunt. To the point. And when it comes to things hockey related, usually right. That is what they told us we’d be getting when the Oilers pulled Babcock out of coaching purgatory this summer, and so far, the advanced billing has been spot on. It’s become a funny place over the years, Edmonton, where the level of deference to the top players has existed on a sliding scale with how good those top players are. No one’s top players are as good as Edmonton’s, and as such, at times they were allowed at times to run amok. A decade without a Stanley Cup provided grounds for reflection, however, and so Connor McDavid , Draisaitl and Zach Hyman somewhat orchestrated the hiring of Babcock, pulling him out of enforced retirement for a job and a paycheck he certainly does not need. “You don't need it, so why do you do it? items.title: McDavid welcomes Hellebuyck’s move east as NHL stars react to blockbuster trade
items.body: The Connor Hellebuyck trade caught the attention of many in the hockey world, with a host of opinions and reactions. The Winnipeg Jets finally parted ways with the three-time Vezina Trophy and Hart Trophy winner Friday, ending months of speculation by trading him to the New Jersey Devils for a package of players and picks. Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid is relieved to see Hellebuyck leave the Western Conference. "He’s a great goalie, a goalie that is a real difference-maker. I am certainly glad he’s gone east,” McDavid said after practice Friday. "You’d hate to see him go somewhere west and have to see him more.” Colorado Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar also seemed content with Hellebuyck being moved out of the Central Division. "Sure, I don't mind," he said with a smile when asked by reporters on Friday. "You knew he was getting traded at some point; you just didn't know where. To see him go to Jersey doesn't hurt my feelings." Buffalo Sabres goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, who had been involved in the Hellebuyck trade rumours, told The Athletic that the deal is going to quiet a lot of conversation around the league." “I mean that’s part of sports, and that’s what makes sports great is that there’s always those conversations and names thrown around, but I think there’s just so much talk about it. Around the league, around our team," Luukkonen said. " I think it’s good for everybody that some of that noise quiets down. items.summary: The purpose of the OHL's showcase event in Cornwall wasn't solely to gauge the market's interest for expansion, but commissioner Bryan Crawford isn't ruling out the possibility of team's being added in the future.

The OHL played a pair of games in Cornwall on the weekend, with the Brampton Steelheads facing off against the Ottawa 67's and Kingston Frontenacs in a neutral-location showcase event. Attendance was decent, considering the locals didn't have any emotional attachment to the teams, but it was also a homecoming for the OHL. "It was a really good first event," said OHL commissioner Bryan Crawford. "The community certainly responded really well - it was amazing to see how prominent and embedded the Cornwall Royals brand is in that community." More Videos Indeed, the old Royals played in major junior for years, first in the QMJHL (Cornwall is close to the provincial border) and then in the OHL before moving to Newmarket and eventually becoming the Sarnia Sting. Royals alumni include titans such as Dale Hawerchuk and Doug Gilmour. When the announcement was first teased, I assumed Cornwall was getting an expansion team. So were these two games a trial run? items.summary: The New Jersey Devils are the winners of the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes, pulling off a big trade with Winnipeg right as the goaltender was scheduled to return to the team. Jason Bukala breaks down both sides of the deal.
items.body: Back in the summer of 2019, Tampa Bay netminder Andrei Vasilevskiy signed an eight-year contract with a $9.5 million cap hit. This was right after he won his first Vezina Trophy, but also right after his Presidents' Trophy-winning Lightning were swept out of the first round by Columbus. He was five years into his career at that point, but already established as one of the best in the game. Still, at the time, a $9.5 million cap hit for a goalie was a lot. Year 1 of his extension would count for 11.66 per cent of the cap, which today would be equivalent to about a $12.1 million AAV. No goalie makes that amount. Seven years later, Vasilevskiy's AAV is still second-highest among goalies, and he's since won two Stanley Cups and another Vezina. Why do we bring this up? Because at the time of Vasilevskiy's signing, our Cap Comparables article analyzing the deal explored the pros and cons of spending so much money on a position with two juxtaposing realities: a) it's the most important position to the success of your hockey club and b) it's the most difficult one to get right. The graveyard of flash-in-the-pan goalies is large, while those worth such a salary are few and far between. We compared the value of NHL goalies to that of an NFL running back. The idea that "running backs don't matter" in football came from evidence that it may not be prudent to pay a premium for the position when the offensive line blocking for them is so important to any runner's success. Of course, this doesn't mean running backs actually don't matter — you can't scheme them out of your game plan. But it's a position to be financially prudent with. items.title: Will the Hellebuyck trade be the Devils’ only big move this season?
items.summary: The Devils took a big swing in acquiring the Hart Trophy winner, but is that going to be it for Sunny Mehta?
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images The New Jersey Devils are being taken very seriously after acquiring Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets. However, will that be the only rabbit general manager Sunny Mehta pulls out of his hat this year? The rookie GM made a big swing in trading a large number of assets to get the Hart Trophy winner. Today, that player is defenseman Daemon Hunt , whom the Wild announced they have placed on waivers. Presumably, Minnesota will assign Hunt to the AHL’s Iowa Wild if he clears. Given that he is strictly a depth defenseman, even at his age, the Wild shouldn’t have any issues passing him through the wire. In the NHL, Hunt has only played for Minnesota. The Wild selected him with the 65th overall pick in the 2020 NHL Draft. Since becoming a full-time professional player for the 2022-23 season, most of Hunt’s professional career has been spent in the Wild organization. Early into the 2024-25 season, Minnesota traded Hunt to the Columbus Blue Jackets as part of the package for David Jiříček . During his tenure with the Blue Jackets organization, he played only for the AHL’s Cleveland Monsters, scoring two goals and 14 points in 48 games with a -8 rating. He re-signed with Columbus the following offseason, but the Wild claimed him off waivers before the regular season. In a similar role, Hunt spent the entire 2025-26 season with Minnesota. He finished the campaign with six assists in 32 games with a -3 rating, averaging 12:26 of ice time per game. This year, Hunt has been held scoreless in 11 contests, while averaging 14:08 of ice time per night. If he is assigned to AHL Iowa after clearing waivers, it’ll be his first AHL appearance since the 2024-25 season.

items.summary: As Winnipeg laments the loss of a franchise legend, Jersey GM Mehta looks like a genius.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The Connor Hellebuyck era is over in Winnipeg . The signature player of the Jets’ second iteration, Hellebuyck won everything but the Stanley Cup in Manitoba, collecting three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy. Hellebuyck had grown vocally discontent with Winnipeg’s lackluster follow-up to a Presidents’ Trophy win in 2024-25, though, having apparently lost confidence that the Jets in front of him could compete as he waded into his late prime. Suspended without pay for skipping camp, ‘Bucky’ crossed the Rubicon and forced an exit from the only organization he’s ever known. An acrimonious end to a brilliant tenure in the prairies opened the door for the New Jersey Devils and GM Sunny Mehta, who had kept his interest in a player his predecessor, Tom Fitzgerald, had long courted close to the vest. The Devils have been searching for a goalie since Corey Schneider’s prime, which, as you may know, was a while ago. They have one now in Hellebuyck, who would walk into the Hall of Fame on his first try if he retired today. Will he do what Jacob Markstrom could not and complete Jersey’s Cup-contention puzzle? The Jets, meanwhile, have needed an out from their reliance on Hellebuyck and a thirtysomething core for some time. That one seed back in 2025 felt like this roster’s last real chance at the Cup during its collective prime, and a scorched-earth rebuild was never on the cards given how closely Winnipeg’s survival as a franchise is tied to its season-ticket sales. That means getting value via trades in lean years, especially for players of Hellebuyck’s quality. Can Dawson Mercer, young Alexander Command, and Co. help the Jets delay their decline? items.body: One thing we can be sure of when evaluating the evolution of NHL hockey is: nobody’s getting less talented. Fourth-line “grinders” have hands that rival your average skill player from the '80s, speed keeps ramping up each year, and goalies keep getting savvier and more athletic. The goalie one is strange, though, because if you solely use what has been used as a major source of evaluation for a long time in our game – save percentage – you might think they’re going the other way. Today, we take a look at the New Jersey Devils outlook after acquiring elite goalie Connor Hellebuyck. The New Jersey Devils acquired Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets on Oct. 23, and the goalie's elite advanced metrics solidify their status as a Stanley Cup contender. The Devils landed Hellebuyck, who's a three-time Vezina Trophy winner (2020, 2024, 2025) and also won the Hart Trophy two seasons ago (2025), without having to trade away any of their core forwards or defensemen and addressed their biggest weakness with the move. The 33-year-old, who was suspended by the Jets prior to the trade after not reporting to training camp and has not played a game this season, is under contract with the Devils until the 2030-31 season. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-USA TODAY Sports Edmonton Oilers’ defenseman Mattias Ekholm will be out at least one week after he suffered an upper-body injury during Thursday’s game against the Carolina Hurricanes , head coach Mike Babcock told reporters after the game. Ekholm, 36, was injured just seconds into the third period after Hurricanes’ forward William Carrier delivered a hit in the Oilers’ end. The Edmonton blueliner appeared to hit his head on the ice and was slow to get up, and his teammates helped him off the ice. Both Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl recorded five points and factored in on all five of Edmonton’s goals. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Seattle’s Chandler Stephenson preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal . items.title: Oilers’ McDavid becomes fourth NHLer ever to register 30 points in first 10 games
items.summary: McDavid joins Mike Bossy, Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux as the only players to achieve the feat after a five-point night.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just when you think you’ve seen it all from Connor McDavid, he continues to one-up himself. During Thursday night’s game against the Carolina Hurricanes , the Edmonton Oilers ‘ captain became the fourth player in NHL history to get 30 points in his first 10 games of a season with a five-point night. McDavid joins some elite company in achieving this feat, as only Mike Bossy, Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux have managed to get 30 points in the first 10 games of a season. Bossy and Gretzky have only achieved the feat once, both doing so in the 1984-85 season, while Lemieux did it three times in 1988-89, 1992-93 and 1995-96, the quickest coming in 1988-89 when he hit 30 points in only eight games. Bossy and Gretzky went on to put up a respective 117 and 208 points in 1984-85, while Lemieux had 199, 160 and 161 in his three respective seasons. This also makes McDavid the first player to achieve this feat in 31 years, and the first to do so in the 21st century. McDavid achieved the feat early in the third period of the game with the secondary assist on the 4-4 goal from Leon Draisaitl. At the start of a power play, McDavid had won the faceoff to Evan Bouchard, and after the Oilers center received a return pass, he then sent the puck across the ice to Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, who set up Draisaitl in front of the net for a one-timer goal. The assist was McDavid’s fourth point in the game, as he had gotten points on all four goals at the time. items.title: Jets fall to Stars in OT for fourth loss in a row
items.body: DALLAS — Roope Hintz scored on a breakaway 3:47 into overtime after his game-tying goal with two minutes left in regulation and the Dallas Stars beat the Winnipeg Jets 3-2 on Thursday night. Wyatt Johnston scored his first goal of the season for Dallas, after 45 last season, and had an assist. Jason Robertson and Mikko Rantanen each had two assists. Rantanen, who two nights earlier had a hat trick for every Stars goal in a 3-2 overtime win against Boston, passed to Hintz from behind the net for the late regulation goal. Hintz had been denied a tying goal at the end of the second period after he got his stick on a puck from the side of the net behind Stuart Skinner, who made an incredible save reaching back with his glove to smother the rolling puck before it could cross the line. Gabriel Vilardi and Kyle Connor scored goals less than two minutes apart in the second period for the Jets, who have lost four one-goal games in a row. Vilardi kept whacking at an unsecured puck that was against the pads of goalie Jake Oettinger, and Connor scored on a one-timer from the middle of the right circle after a turnover. Oettinger stopped 17 shots, and has allowed two goals or less in seven of his eight games this season. Jets forward Nino Niederreiter left the ice bleeding with 6:51 left in the game after taking a stick to the face from teammate Tyrel Bauer. Robertson got his 500th and 501st career points (216 goals, 285 assists) in his 466th game. Only three players in Stars franchise history reached 500 points in fewer games — Neal Broten (461), Bobby Smith (463) and Dino Ciccarelli (465). items.summary: The Edmonton Oilers will be holding their breath on the status of one of their best defencemen.
items.body: The Edmonton Oilers will be holding their breath on the status of one of their best defencemen. Mattias Ekholm was forced to exit early in the third period of Thursday's game against the Carolina Hurricanes after a collision with William Carrier. As Ekholm played the puck out in his own end, Carrier caught the Oilers defenceman with a big hit. As Ekholm fell, his head appeared to hit the ice. He stayed on his knees as he was attended to by the trainers. Ekholm eventually got to his feet and made his way off the ice, but appeared unsteady and needed assistance from teammates. The Oilers quickly ruled Ekholm out for the remainder of the contest. Ekholm, 36, entered Thursday's game with one goal and two assists in nine games.

items.title: Connor McDavid becomes fourth player to record 30 points in first 10 games
items.body: The Edmonton Oilers star became just the fourth player in NHL history to record 30 points in the first 10 games of the season when he notched his fourth point of the evening in the third period against the Carolina Hurricanes. The assist on Leon Draisaitl's power-play goal was his third of the night, giving McDavid 23 for the season. His goal earlier in the night was his seventh of the campaign. McDavid's third consecutive multi-point night now puts him on an early pace for 252 points for the season. Wayne Gretzky and Mike Bossy both had 30 points in the first 10 games of 1984-85, while Mario Lemieux accomplished the feat three times (1988-89, 1992-93 and 1995-96). items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images The Toronto Maple Leafs have announced that defenseman Marshall Rifai will be placed on injured reserve and will be week-to-week with a lower-body injury. It’s unclear what the cause of the injury was, as Rifai played the entirety of Tuesday’s 6-2 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets , getting a shift as late as the 19:36 mark of the third period. He was at morning skate ahead of Thursday’s 5-4 win over the New York Rangers , but left early, with Leafs head coach Jim Hiller telling the media that he was “dealing with something”. Rifai was also not present for warmups for Thursday’s game, confirming his absence, and then the team announced the injury after the win. Rifai’s week-to-week timeline indicates that he won’t be available for the upcoming road trip in the Northwest, although it’s unclear how much time he’ll miss beyond that. His IR placement also confirms that he will miss the next three games, unless the placement was retroactive to his last instance of game action on Tuesday, then it would just be the upcoming two before he’s eligible to be taken off IR. Rifai is mainly a regular for the Leafs’ AHL affiliate, the Toronto Marlies, but was on the NHL roster as an injury replacement for Chris Tanev, who is also week-to-week. Rifai only managed to get into two games before sustaining the injury, scoring his first career NHL goal in Tuesday’s win . He had also gone pointless in three AHL games with the Marlies. With Rifai and Tanev out, the Leafs will likely roll with the six-man defense corps of Nick Blankenburg, Oliver Ekman-Larsson, Jake McCabe, Darren Raddysh, Morgan Rielly and Troy Stecher for the most part. items.title: Stecher scores in final minute to lift Maple Leafs over Rangers
items.body: TORONTO — Troy Stecher scored with 26.3 seconds left in regulation as the Toronto Maple Leafs topped the New York Rangers 5-4 in a back-and-forth affair for their third straight victory Thursday. Brandon Duhaime, with a goal and two assists, Teddy Blueger, Kirill Marchenko and Easton Cowan provided the rest of the offence for Toronto (6-4-2). Sergei Bobrovsky made 21 saves. Zack MacEwen added two assists. Blueger also had an assist for a two-point night. Mika Zibanejad, with a goal and an assist, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Tye Kartye and Alexis Lafrenière replied for New York (7-4-1), which got 31 stops from Dylan Garand. Adam Fox chipped in four assists. Stecher's winner came on a delayed penalty after he took a pass from Morgan Rielly and ripped a shot upstairs. After the teams traded goals inside the game's first six minutes, Blueger put Toronto ahead with his first for the club at 10:01 on a shot that just dribbled over the line. New York evened things 2-2 at 2:37 of the second when Bjorkstrand beat Bobrovsky from in tight. The visitors nudged in front at 6:30 when Kartye tipped home a point shot, but Duhaime buried his own rebound 90 seconds later — also his first goal in blue and white — to get Toronto level again. Marchenko gave the home side the lead with 50 seconds left in the period on a power play, but Lafrenière knotted the score again at 14:25 of the third. Bobrovsky tied Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist for the most wins by a non-North American goaltender with 459. The pair now share sixth on the all-time list. items.body: OTTAWA — The San Jose Sharks picked up their first regulation win of the season Thursday night with a 6-2 win over the Ottawa Senators . Colin Graf led the way with a goal and an assist. Nolan Allan, Tyler Toffoli, Jacob Trouba, Zack Ostapchuk and Ivar Stenberg also scored for the Sharks (6-4-1). Tim Stutzle and Jordan Spence tallied for the Senators (7-4-0). Samuel Ersson, who made 23 saves, remains in search of his first win with Ottawa. Ottawa placed Linus Ullmark on injured reserve Thursday after he suffered a lower-body injury a night earlier. Spence scored at 6:24 of the third period to make it a two-goal game. The Senators pulled Ersson while on the power play with under four minutes remaining but Ostapchuk took advantage of a giveaway and scored an empty-net goal. Stenberg added a second empty-netter to round out the scoring. Senators: Ottawa lacked the intensity it played with Wednesday against the Panthers and couldn’t bury its chances. Sharks: San Jose played a solid road game and capitalized on its opportunities. Toffoli broke a 1-1 tie at the halfway mark of the second period by getting a shot through traffic from the point on the power play. Sharks: San Jose travels to Boston to take on the Bruins on Saturday.

items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Arseny Gritsyuk and Nico Hischier scored first-period goals, Nico Daws made 16 saves and the New Jersey Devils beat the Anaheim Ducks 4-1 on Thursday night. items.title: Save of the Season? Sharks' Askarov makes diving glove save to rob goal
items.summary:
Dive save and a beauty.
San Jose Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made an incredible diving glove save to stop a sure goal off a rocket from Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday.
The Senators had a man advantage with defenseman Jake Sanderson controlling the puck
items.body: San Jose Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made an incredible diving glove save to stop a sure goal off a rocket from Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday. The Senators had a man advantage with defenseman Jake Sanderson controlling the puck at the point. Sanderson went cross-ice to forward Tim Stutzle at the right circle. Askarov moved to his left to play a shot from Stutzle, but he opted to go back across the ice to Batherson, who had a pretty open net. Askarov, a right-hand catcher, made a huge dive to his right and snagged Batherson's shot out of midair. Even with some traffic in front of the net, Askarov was still able to get there with the dive, looking more like a Gold Glove shortstop than a hockey goalie. Earlier in the game, Askarov made a pretty nice pad save on a Shane Pinto breakaway chance. After the diving save, he laid on the ice for a second and waited for the whistle. Take the rest, Yaroslav. You earned it.

items.title: Golden Knights’ Mitch Marner to miss game vs. Blues for birth of child
items.summary: The 29-year-old and his wife Stephanie Marner are set to welcome their second child.
items.body: Forward Mitch Marner will be unavailable for the Vegas Golden Knights on the road for their Thursday night game against the St. Louis Blues as he and his partner, Stephanie Marner, await the birth of their second child. The team confirmed his status ahead of puck drop, after the Las Vegas Review-Journal reported that Marner and his wife were expecting the newborn. The Marner’s first child was born in May 2025, Miles Daniel Marner, with the birth happening just before Game 1 of the round two Stanley Cup Playoff series against the Florida Panthers, when Mitch was still a member of the Toronto Maple Leafs. Now in his second season with the Golden Knights, the 29-year-old Marner has a pair of goals and 10 assists for 11 points in 11 regular season games this season, as he looks to build on his 24 goals, 56 assists and 80-point campaign from last season’s 81 games and eventual advancement to the Stanley Cup Final. In his place for Thursday’s contest, Alexander Holtz is set to draw into the lineup for his NHL season debut. The 24-year-old native of Stockholm, Sweden, played in 28 games with the Golden Knights last season, scoring three goals and six assists for nine points. This season, he has enjoyed a strong start in the AHL with the Henderson Silver Knights, scoring four goals and four assists for eight points in eight games. Vegas enter Thursday’s road matchup with the Blues sitting first in the Western Conference’s Pacific Division with an 8-3-0 record, and will be back on the ice on the road against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday night before returning home to T-Mobile Arena for a pair of home games next week against the Ottawa Senators and New Jersey Devils .

items.title: Red Wings looking for young centres in trade talks
items.body: The Detroit Red Wings appear to be letting teams know what it could take to acquire their two unhappy superstars. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Thursday's episode of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast that the Red Wings are seeking young centres in trade talks for Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson . "Detroit, whatever they're considering out there, whether it's Larkin or Edvinsson ... but the one thing I think they are doing, and I've heard this a little bit, is they're starting to ask about young centres. And maybe some guys who are top prospects who aren't in the NHL yet. I had a couple of teams tell me on Wednesday ... whatever Detroit is planning here, they're looking at young centres." Friedman added that he couldn't say if the conversations were related to Larkin, Edvinsson or both. "I've had a couple of teams say to me do not be surprised if and when this logjam breaks, if one or two (centres) are involved for Detroit if they can. That is definitely a goal of theirs," he said. Larkin, 30, is a centre who has been on the market since he requested a trade at the end of last season. He holds a no-trade clause but a recent report from The Detroit Free Press revealed that the former Red Wings captain has expanded the list of teams he is open to joining to 10. The Red Wings have had trouble building centre depth behind Larkin over the course of their 10-year playoff drought. Currently the team is leaning heavily on Andrew Copp and Larkin, while sophomore Emmitt Finnie has moved from wing to centre. Meanwhile, recent first-round picks Marco Kasper and Nate Danielson have had their development slowed by injuries and neither is contributing to the team right now. items.body: Register Login East Notes: Chatfield, Cousins, Tkachuk By Ethan Hetu | at October 22, 2026 6:35 pm The Carolina Hurricanes did a remarkable job retaining nearly the entirety of their Stanley Cup-winning roster from last season. But with another year set to go by, it seems almost certain that the club will lose at least some players from their championship roster. One player that could depart is pending UFA defenseman Jalen Chatfield . David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period reported yesterday that the Hurricanes and Chatfield’s agent, Darren Ferris of Quartexx, attempted to negotiate an extension, but those talks did not result in pen hitting paper. Pagnotta noted that there “have been no talks since” between Ferris and the Hurricanes, and added that the “inkling right now is that [Chatfield] is headed to free agency.” Chatfield, could be set to cash in on the open market after becoming a steady contributor to the Hurricanes’ defense over the last half-decade. A fleet-footed undrafted blueliner, Chatfield was plucked from the Canucks organization as a free agent and broke into the NHL after one season spent developing with Carolina’s AHL affiliate, the Chicago Wolves. After winning a Calder Cup in Chicago, Chatfield established himself at the NHL level. He was a seamless fit for the way head coach Rod Brind’Amour wants his defensemen to play, and his ability to leverage his above-average skating to close out on pucks quickly and play aggressively has made him a valuable secondary defensive piece for the club. Now 30 years old, Chatfield’s upcoming free agency represents his best chance at earning a life-changing contract. Based on Pagnotta’s reporting, it seems Chatfield might end up receiving that contract, just maybe not from the Hurricanes.

items.title: Panthers’ Cooper Black becomes tallest goalie to play NHL game
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Florida Panthers goalie Cooper Black skated onto the PPG Paints Arena ice alone during pregame warmups on Thursday night, a time-honoured hockey tradition given to rookies everywhere. It took Black fewer strides to make the memorable lap than most. Black made NHL history in his first career start when he became the tallest goaltender to ever appear in a regular-season game. Black is listed as two inches taller than Ben Bishop, Ivan Fedotov, Mads Sogaard and Mikko Koskinen, all 6-foot-7. The 25-year-old from Alpen, Michigan, who started playing when he was 8 and had a 5-inch growth spurt between his junior and senior years in high school when he shot up from 6 feet to 6 feet 5 inches and kept right on going, was excellent in his first period. Black, called up from Florida's AHL affiliate in Charlotte recently after Jacob Markstrom went down with a shoulder injury, stopped Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman Kris Letang with his blocker pad on a wrist shot about two minutes in. He also turned aside a breakaway opportunity by Penguins forward Rickard Rakell before giving up a goal to Nick Robertson, who beat Black to the glove side. Panthers head coach Paul Maurice praised Black's development in recent years. Florida signed Black as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. Black blossomed last season in Charlotte, posting a 25-13-4 record with a 2.47 goals against average and a .903 save percentage. “A man that size, it takes a long time to grow into that body,” Maurice said before adding with a laugh, “I think he’s done.”

items.body: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports Remembering The Life And Legacy Of Rangers Star Ron Duguay Ken Campbell Partner Oct 22, 2026 8:15 PM Published Oct 22, 2026 8:15 PM Updated Oct 22, 2026 8:55 PM The 12-year NHL star has passed away after a long battle with cancer. Most hockey fans remember Ron Duguay as a the perfectly coiffed cult star of the New York Rangers . And he deserves all of the recognition he gets as one of the most popular players in franchise history. But Duguay, who died of cancer at the age of 69 on Wednesday, was even more popular and dynamic as a member of the Sudbury Wolves in the mid-1970s, when he led a team that did everything but win an Ontario League championship. That was where he first displayed his blazing speed, on-ice elegance and soft touch before being drafted by the Rangers in the first round of the 1977 draft. And even though he's not in the Hockey Hall of Fame, those of us from Northern Ontario will always look fondly at his No. 10, which hangs in the rafters of the Sudbury Arena.

Alex Semin , who officially retired from professional hockey himself in May 2022 , recently spoke with Match TV’s Pavel Lysenkov about Ovechkin’s big announcement . The two were teammates with the Washington Capitals for six seasons (2006-2012) and formed a close bond as the two Russian-speaking members of Washington’s star quartet of “Young Guns.” “I don’t think it was a secret to anyone,” Semin said , as translated via Google Translate. “The question was whether he would play (this season) at all. But there’s still one more milestone left. I think he’ll break it and, so to speak, retire with a clear conscience.” The milestone Semin refers to is Wayne Gretzky’s combined regular-season and postseason goals record, which stands at 1,016 goals. With his goal against the Seattle Kraken earlier this month, Ovechkin (1,007) is now just nine goals away from tying Gretzky for the top spot. Ovechkin started the 2026-27 campaign with the slowest goal-scoring pace of his 22-year career, with one marker in his first nine games, but Semin remains confident his countryman will get the job done. “Although with every goal it gets harder and harder,” Semin said. “Of course, we’re not getting any younger. But I think Sasha can handle this task. He’s used to such challenges. Everyone said it was impossible, but it turned out to be possible.” Ovechkin’s pursuit of those remaining goals will likely be aided by the Capitals’ big-time roster strengthening this past offseason. items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Listening To Trade Offers For Dmitri Voronkov By Ethan Hetu | at October 22, 2026 2:45 pm The Columbus Blue Jackets are listening to trade offers for winger Dmitri Voronkov as “some teams” have been calling with interest in the player, reports Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic . This development comes as Voronkov has “run aground” with the Blue Jackets, according to LeBrun’s colleague at The Athletic, Aaron Portzline . Voronkov was a healthy scratch for Columbus’ slate of back-to-back games on Oct. 17 and 18, before returning to the lineup for the club’s loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday. Most recently, Voronkov skated on the Blue Jackets’ second line, alongside countryman Valeri Nichushkin and veteran No. 2 center Sean Monahan . Previously, Voronkov had battled with 22-year-old Luca Del Bel Belluz for a spot on Columbus’ fourth line. So far this season, Voronkov is averaging just 11:44 time on ice per game, including usage on the club’s second power play unit. In terms of production, he’s managed two assists in six games and is still waiting on his first goal. This is not the first time the 26-year-old has found himself battling for regular ice time in the Blue Jackets’ lineup. Voronkov’s NHL career, which is now in its fourth year, has been something of a rollercoaster, defined by its highs and lows. At his best, Voronkov has looked like a core part of the team’s future. As a rookie, Voronkov managed 18 goals and 34 points, translating his success from the KHL seamlessly to the NHL.
